title: MakeMyTrip Technical Interview — Complete Prep Guide
intro: Compiled from GFG, LeetCode Discuss, Glassdoor, Naukri Code360 — 2019–2025. DSA answers in C++. Backend/LLD/HLD answers in Java / Spring Boot / MySQL.

process.title: Online Assessment (HackerEarth/HackerRank)
process.desc: 22 questions = 2 algorithmic coding + 20 MCQs covering DBMS, OS, CN, Java OOP, SQL, aptitude. Medium difficulty.

process.title: DSA / Problem Solving Round (60 min)
process.desc: 2 coding questions — arrays, linked lists, trees, DP, graphs. LeetCode Easy–Medium. Working code + dry-run + complexity required.

process.title: LLD / Machine Coding Round (60 min)
process.desc: Design and code a real system in Java. SOLID principles, design patterns, concurrency are tested hands-on. Java is a hard requirement.

process.title: HLD / System Design Round (60–90 min)
process.desc: Distributed, travel-domain-relevant systems. DB schema, SQL, scalability, concurrency, caching, microservices.

process.title: Managerial / Director Round (SDE-2+)
process.desc: Project depth, innovative contributions, latency problems solved, architecture decisions. Prepare STAR stories from production.

overviewWarn.title: ⚠️ MMT-Specific Signals
overviewWarn.body: Java is a hard requirement — even if DSA is in Python/C++, expect Java follow-ups (records, streams, concurrency). SOLID principles and design patterns tested live in LLD. Idempotency and double-payment prevention are very commonly asked.

tipBoxes.title: 🎯 MMT Core Requirements
tipBoxes.body: (1) Java is mandatory even if you code DSA in C++. (2) Concurrency appears in every round. (3) Design patterns live-coded in LLD — State, Builder, Adapter, Observer are the most common. (4) Idempotency & double-payment — must have a crisp answer for this. (5) Production-readiness: every design decision needs trade-off rationale.

tipSections.title: DSA Priority List
items: Must know (🔥 High freq): Sliding Window, Two Pointer, HashMap prefix-sum, Merge K sorted, Jump Game, LCA, LRU, FreqStack, Longest Consecutive Sequence, Permutations
Should know (⚡ Med): Dijkstra, Tarjan bridges, DP (MSIS, Dice throw), Multiply strings, Sort by frequency
Nice to know: Josephus, Tower of Hanoi, coordinate GCD, vertical tree traversal

tipSections.title: Java Checklist
items: ✅ HashMap internals: capacity 16, load factor 0.75, bitmask hash & (n-1)
✅ Concurrency: volatile vs synchronized vs Atomic — know when to use each, live
✅ CompletableFuture: supplyAsync, thenApply, thenCompose, exceptionally, join
✅ @Transactional propagation: REQUIRED vs REQUIRES_NEW — self-invocation pitfall
✅ Spring Interceptors vs Filters — difference and use cases
✅ Optional (Java 8); Records (16+); sealed classes (17+)

tipSections.title: DSA Strategy
items: Priority topics: Arrays+Strings (Sliding Window, Two Pointer), Linked Lists, Trees (BFS/DFS/LCA), DP (subsequence patterns), Graphs (BFS/Dijkstra/Bridges), Heaps
Solve 2 questions per round — expect 60 mins per coding round. Budget 25 mins per question.
Always start with brute force → then optimise. MMT interviewers appreciate the thought process over jumping to optimal.
Always analyse time and space complexity. Do a dry-run on a sample test case when asked.
For LeetCode prep: focus on Medium difficulty. Hard is rarely asked; Easy is used only as warmup at senior levels.
Recommended list: LeetCode Top 100 Liked + all problems tagged "MakeMyTrip" on LeetCode

tipSections.title: Java Preparation Checklist
items: ✅ Java 8–17: Streams, Optional (8+), Records (16+), sealed classes (17+)
✅ HashMap internals: hashing, load factor, rehashing, why size is power of 2
✅ Concurrency: synchronized, volatile, AtomicXxx, ReentrantLock, Semaphore, CountDownLatch
✅ ExecutorService: ThreadPoolExecutor, CompletableFuture, ForkJoinPool
✅ Collections: ConcurrentHashMap vs HashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList
✅ Garbage Collection: G1GC basics, when to worry about GC pauses
✅ Spring: bean lifecycle, @Transactional propagation, AOP, interceptors
✅ Practice coding design patterns live in Java — not just knowing them theoretically

tipSections.title: System Design Preparation
items: ✅ Go deep on: Ticket Booking (concurrency, optimistic locking), URL Shortener, Rate Limiter, Distributed Cache
✅ Know the trade-offs: SQL vs NoSQL, REST vs gRPC vs Kafka, sync vs async
✅ Practice DB schema design: normalisation, indexing, query optimisation
✅ Idempotency keys, outbox pattern, and saga are table-stakes for payments/booking domain
✅ Be ready to defend every decision — Why this DB? Why this cache strategy? What breaks at 10x load?

tipSections.title: MMT-Specific Resume Prep (SDE-2+)
items: Prepare 3 STAR stories: one latency fix, one architecture change you proposed, one innovative feature you shipped
For every tech in your resume (Redis, Kafka, Elasticsearch): know why you chose it, what alternatives existed, what trade-offs were made
Quantify achievements: "reduced API response time by 98%" is exactly what MMT probes on
Know your Spring Boot microservice flow end-to-end: request → controller → service → repository → DB → cache
Be ready for: "Describe a production incident and how you debugged it" with Kibana/Grafana as tools

tipWarn.title: ⚠️ Top Rejection Reasons at MMT
items: Using synchronized everywhere in LLD — interviewers want Atomic / non-blocking alternatives
Not using State pattern in Vending Machine LLD
No clear idempotency answer for double-payment scenario
Weak Java internals despite Spring Boot on resume
No production STAR stories for Director-level managerial round
